stem: An applicant for Massachusetts pharmacist licensure submits a birth record under a former surname and uses a current married surname on the application. The applicant otherwise appears eligible but does not include written notice of the name change. What is the best assessment?

choices.text: The applicant should provide written notice of the name change because substantive eligibility does not cure an incomplete application.
The application is complete because the Board must infer the name change from the different surnames.
A current government-issued photo identification automatically replaces the required birth record and written name-change notice for all licensure purposes.
The discrepancy matters only after the applicant passes all required examinations.
The applicant must abandon the current surname and apply only under the surname shown on the birth record.

explanation.core_reasoning: The licensure application must be fully and correctly completed and must include proof of birth. When the applicant's current name differs from the name on the birth record, written notice of the name change is required. Meeting substantive eligibility criteria does not make the submission complete, and the Board may decline to consider an improperly completed application.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the written name-change notice is part of completing the application, separately from whether the applicant is otherwise eligible.
choice_analysis.B: The application must supply the required written notice; the Board need not infer the explanation for the mismatch.
choice_analysis.C: Photo identification does not eliminate the separate birth-record and name-change-documentation requirements.
choice_analysis.D: Application completeness is relevant when the application is submitted and is not postponed until after examinations.
choice_analysis.E: The rule calls for written notice of the name change, not abandonment of the applicant's current legal name.

related_facts: The Board may refuse to consider an application that is not properly completed.
Application completeness and substantive examination eligibility are distinct inquiries.
explanation.mpje_trap: A plausible explanation for a surname mismatch is not the same as supplying the written documentation the application rule requires.

reasoning_steps: Compare the current application name with the birth record
Identify the missing written name-change notice
Treat application completeness separately from substantive eligibility
